usecases.title: Live sales dashboard
usecases.description: Shows today's, this week's and this month's sales invoices and returns by customer, salesman, item and store, refreshed through the day, so the owner sees revenue without waiting for an accountant's report.
data: sales invoices (type 9) and sales returns (type 4): header date, customer_code, salesman, currency, rate, discount, balance, vat (p. 13)
invoice lines: code, unit, store, quantity, price, bonus, discount (p. 14)
customer names and item names/groups for grouping (pp. 7, 9–10)
store names (p. 6)
usecases.why: Voucher/GetVouchers filters only by customerCode, currencyCode, fromDate and toDate (p. 17), with no voucher-type, salesman or store filter and no paging, so each refresh downloads every voucher in the date range and keeps types 9 and 4 client-side; which Voucher class it returns and whether header balance is net of discount are not stated (pp. 13, 17).

usecases.title: Customer 360 view
usecases.description: One screen per customer with contact details, assigned salesman, price class, credit limit, current balance, balances per currency, unpaid and returned cheque totals, classifications, GPS location and the serial-numbered goods they bought.
data: customer card: code, name, phone, street, street2, salesman_code, price_class, credit_limit, discount, VATReg, stopped, latitude, longitude, paymentTermsCode (p. 7)
balance, notPayedCheqsBalance, returnedCheqsBalance with getBalance (p. 7)
classifications and contacts with getClassifications / getContacts (pp. 7–8)
per-currency balances: code, pos, currency, date, balance, rate (p. 8)
the customer's serials and warranty dates via the customer header (pp. 11–12)
usecases.why: Every section uses documented headers and fields of GetCustomers (pp. 6–8), GetCustomerBalances (p. 8) and GetItemsSerials (pp. 11–12); the caveats are that fields such as attr, creditType and citizen_code are undocumented and the manual does not say whether balance already includes the cheque balances (p. 7).

usecases.title: Customer statement sender & portal
usecases.description: Produces a customer's account statement for any period as a PDF or WhatsApp message, or lets a trusted customer open their own statement online, replacing manual statement requests to the accountant.
data: statement rows: date, code, type, credit, debit, start_date, balance, note (p. 13)
filters: customerCode, currencyCode, fromDate, toDate, showOtherCurrencies, showStocks, showCheqs, showNotPayedCheqs, showReturnedCheq (p. 12)
customer name, phone and current balance (p. 7)
usecases.why: Report/GetAccountsheet is documented (pp. 12–13), but credit, debit and balance come back as strings in an unstated number format and start_date and type have no stated meaning, so totals must be parsed defensively; a customer-facing portal also relies on Bawaba scoping each token to one customer, because the API's only login is a Shamel user (p. 4).

usecases.title: Order status tracker
usecases.description: Lets office staff (or customers through a WhatsApp bot) check whether a sales order is not ready, ready, closed, partly sent or sent, using the order's paper reference number.
data: order status 0 not ready, 1 ready, 2 closed, 3 sent partially, 4 sent (p. 16)
order header and lines for display (p. 17)
usecases.why: GetStatus takes only Header[manual] (presumably the order's manual_code, inferred) and returns the 0–4 status (p. 16), so orders entered without a manual_code cannot be looked up, and the response format and the result for an unknown or shared manual code are undocumented; automatic 'your order is ready' messages need Bawaba's M3 order.status_changed events.

usecases.title: New-customer onboarding form
usecases.description: A form for salesmen or office staff to register a new customer (name, VAT number, phones, address, city, salesman, level, price class) that first checks for an existing customer with the same VAT number and then creates the account in Shamel.
data: write fields Name, VatReg, Address, MobileNumber, PhoneNumber, Salesman, Street, City, Town, Referee, RefereeMobile, CustomerLevel, PriceClass (p. 9)
new customer code returned in PostResponse.value (p. 9)
duplicate check through the vatreg header (p. 7)
usecases.why: Customer/Post inserts a customer and returns the new code (pp. 8–9), but the write model has no currency, credit limit or discount, MobileNumber is commented 'فاكس' (fax), Town has no lookup list, a mistake cannot be corrected because there is no update endpoint, and whether a retried insert creates a duplicate is unknown.

usecases.title: Multi-store stock view
usecases.description: Shows how much of each item is on hand in every store and van, with shelf locations, so sales and warehouse staff can answer 'where do we have it?' instantly.
data: item_code, store, qnty, shelf, main_unit per item per store (p. 11)
one item with all its stores via getItemDetails: itm, itmStores (p. 11)
store id, name, type, car_code, orgnization_code (p. 6)
usecases.why: GetItemsStores and getItemDetails return quantity per store with shelf and main unit (pp. 10–11) and GetStores names the stores (p. 6); the open points are only about interpretation: that qnty is in the main unit, whether it nets off open orders, and what store type and car_code mean.

usecases.title: Low-stock alerts & reorder suggestions
usecases.title_ar: تنبيهات نقص المخزون واقتراحات إعادة الطلب
usecases.description: Watches stock levels against minimum quantities the company sets per item and store, alerts the purchasing person by email or WhatsApp, and suggests reorder quantities from recent sales.
data: current qnty per item and store (p. 11)
item names, groups, stopped and paused flags (pp. 9–10)
recent sales quantities from invoice lines for sales velocity (pp. 14, 17)
minimum and reorder levels, kept in the tool itself
usecases.why: Quantities are documented (pp. 10–11), but the item model has no minimum or reorder level (pp. 9–10), so thresholds must live in the tool, and the lastupdatedate header of GetItemsStores is listed without any explanation (p. 10), so near-real-time alerts mean re-reading the whole stock list until Bawaba's M3 stock.changed events take over.

usecases.title: Price lookup tool
usecases.description: Answers 'what is the price of this item for this customer?' by combining the six price-class prices, the customer's price class, customer-specific special prices and discounts, and the last prices at which the item was sold.
data: sale_parice1..sale_parice6 and curr1..curr6 per item, unit1..unit6 and unit relations (pp. 9–10)
the 6 price class names (p. 6)
customer price_class (p. 7)
special price rows: price_class_name, customer_code, stock_code, discount, discount_type, price, currency_code, main_unit, tax (pp. 16–17)
last prices: date, code, price, currency, quantity, bonus, unit, customer (p. 12)
usecases.why: All the data is readable, but the link between price class N and sale_pariceN is inferred and unit_price_1..6 and discount_type are undocumented (pp. 6, 9–10, 16–17); GetCustomerPricesAsRows has no documented inputs, so every lookup downloads the whole price table, and GetLastPriceReport has no customer filter (p. 12).

usecases.title: Serial & warranty lookup
usecases.description: Lets service staff type or scan a serial number and see which item it is, which store holds it and when its warranty starts and ends, or list all serial-numbered goods sold to a customer.
data: name, itemCode, serial, status, store, start_grantee_date, end_grantee_date (p. 12)
filters: customer, serial (pp. 11–12)
item details through the serial header of GetItems (p. 9)
usecases.why: GetItemsSerials is documented with customer and serial filters and warranty start and end dates (pp. 11–12); only the status values are undocumented, and the response has no customer field, so the buyer is known only when searching by customer.

usecases.title: Warehouse app: receiving, transfers, goods issue and counts
usecases.title_ar: تطبيق المستودع: الاستلام والتحويل والإخراج والجرد
usecases.description: Handheld app for storekeepers to record goods received from suppliers, transfers between stores and vans, and goods issued, and to count stock and compare it with the book quantity.
data: purchase delivery (type 2), internal delivery (type 16) and stock-out (type 12) vouchers (p. 15)
voucher lines: code, unit, store, quantity (p. 14)
book quantities per store for stock counts (p. 11)
usecases.why: The three voucher types are in VoucherTypes (p. 15), but PurchaseDelivery has no code prefix letter (pp. 15–16), the manual does not say how an internal delivery names its destination store or which fields each type requires, and none of the 13 documented types is a stock-in or adjustment (p. 15), so a count can post only shortages (as type 12).

usecases.title: New items from a supplier price sheet
usecases.title_ar: إنشاء أصناف جديدة من قائمة أسعار المورّد
usecases.description: Reads a supplier's Excel or PDF price list, matches its lines to existing items by barcode or factory code, and creates the missing items in Shamel with name, main unit, price, group and barcode.
data: existing items with barcode, factory_code, orginal_code (pp. 9–10)
item group tree: code, name, parentCode, level (p. 11)
write fields code, unit1, name, type, price1, currency, group, barcode, original_code, factory_code, trademark, producing_company, style, model, note (p. 20)
usecases.why: Item/Post inserts an item (pp. 19–20) but takes only the main unit and one price (price1); trademark, producing_company, style and model are numbers with no lookup list, item type values and the content of PostResponse.value are not stated, and whether a duplicate code is rejected is unknown.

usecases.title: Bulk price & item updates
usecases.description: Would let the company raise prices by a percentage, apply a supplier's new costs, or fix names and barcodes for many items at once from a spreadsheet.
data: current prices sale_parice1..sale_parice6 and item details (pp. 9–10), readable but not writable
usecases.why: The API has no update endpoint for items or anything else: Item/Post is documented only as 'Insert new Item' (pp. 19–20), so existing prices and item details can only be changed in the Shamel desktop program, and a tool can at most prepare a change list for staff to key in.

usecases.title: Collections & credit control board
usecases.description: Ranks customers by what they owe, flags those over their credit limit or with returned cheques, and estimates how old each debt is, so collectors and salesmen know whom to call first.
data: balance, notPayedCheqsBalance, returnedCheqsBalance, credit_limit, stopped, salesman_code, paymentTermsCode (p. 7)
per-currency balances (p. 8)
statement rows to age the balance (p. 13)
voucher amounts with customer_balance_at_voucher_date (p. 18)
usecases.why: Balances and credit limits are documented (pp. 7–8), but there is no aging or overdue report and vouchers carry no due date (only the customer's paymentTermsCode, which has no lookup list), so 'overdue' must be estimated from statement rows whose amounts are strings (p. 13), and whether balance includes cheques is not stated.

usecases.title: Cheque tracker
usecases.description: Lists post-dated cheques received from customers by due date, bank and branch, and shows each customer's totals of not-yet-paid and returned (bounced) cheques, so finance can plan deposits and chase bounced cheques.
data: notPayedCheqsBalance and returnedCheqsBalance per customer with getBalance (p. 7)
cheque lines in vouchers: cheq_num, account_num, bank_code, branch_code, due_date, rate, currency, amount (p. 14)
statement with showCheqs, showNotPayedCheqs, showReturnedCheq (p. 12)
bank and branch names (p. 5)
usecases.why: Per-customer totals of unpaid and returned cheques are documented (p. 7) and individual cheques with due dates appear inside vouchers (p. 14), but no endpoint lists cheques or gives a cheque's status (deposited, cleared, returned), so cheques must be collected by scanning GetVouchers by date (p. 17) and their status inferred from statements.

usecases.title: Currency rate board
usecases.description: Shows the currencies defined in Shamel (the manual's examples are "NIS" and "$") with the latest exchange rates, and keeps its own history so quotes and reports convert amounts consistently.
data: id, code, currency_name, units, division (pp. 4–5)
currency_code, rate, date, is_base for the latest 10 rates (p. 5)
usecases.why: Both endpoints are documented (pp. 4–5); GetCurrencyRates returns only the 'latest 10' rates with no date or currency filter, so a longer history must be recorded by the tool itself, and is_base is not explained.

usecases.title: Automated journal entries & credit/debit notes
usecases.title_ar: قيود يومية وإشعارات دائنة ومدينة آلية
usecases.description: Posts recurring or bulk accounting entries (bank charges, salaries, allocations) and customer credit or debit notes from a spreadsheet or another system, entered as unposted so an accountant reviews them in Shamel.
data: journal (type 28), credit note (type 22) and debit note (type 23) vouchers (p. 15)
accounts lines: position, account_code, amount, debit_credit, costcenter1..costcenter6, note (pp. 14–15)
is_posted flag to enter a voucher as not posted (p. 13)
refrenceId of the created voucher (p. 15)
new cost centers when needed: code, name, name_en, father, type, date (p. 18)
usecases.why: Journal vouchers are supported and accounts is mandatory for them (p. 13), but debit_credit values are undocumented, no endpoint lists GL accounts or cost centers, and a wrong entry cannot be edited or deleted through the API (all writes are inserts), so account codes must come from the accountant and every post needs a reversal plan.

usecases.title: Cost-center reporting
usecases.description: Reports movements per cost center (for example a branch, vehicle or project) for any period, so the owner sees which part of the business makes or loses money.
data: filters fromCostcenter, toCostcenter, account, type, currencyCode, fromDate, toDate, showOtherCurrencies (p. 19)
rows: date, code, type, credit, debit, start_date, balance, note (p. 19)
usecases.why: The cost-center statement is documented (p. 19), but no endpoint lists cost centers, the int type filter and the account filter are unexplained, and amounts are strings, so the tool needs cost-center codes from the accountant and defensive number parsing; creating new cost centers (/CostCenter/Post) is a separate M2 write that returns no identifier (pp. 18–19).

usecases.title: Financial statements, cash position & supplier payables
usecases.description: Would show profit and loss, a trial balance, cash and bank balances and what the company owes each supplier, directly from Shamel.
data: no general-ledger, chart-of-accounts, cash/bank or supplier endpoint exists
usecases.why: The manual offers only three reports, the customer account statement, last prices and the cost-center statement (p. 3), with no chart of accounts, trial balance, P&L, bank balance or supplier list, and no purchase-invoice type among the documented VoucherTypes (p. 15); GetAccountsheet's customerCode might accept other account codes, but that is unconfirmed (p. 12).

usecases.title: Salesman order-entry app
usecases.description: Mobile app where each salesman sees only their own customers, with balance, prices and stock, and enters sales orders and returns on the spot instead of on paper; selected orders can wait for owner approval in Bawaba before reaching Shamel.
data: the salesman's own customers (default GetCustomers scoping, p. 7)
order (type 0) header: customer_code, salesman, manual_code, order_store, date_to_deliver, time_to_deliver (p. 13)
lines: code, unit, store, quantity, price, bonus, discount percentage (p. 14)
sales return (type 4) (p. 15)
refrenceId of the created voucher (p. 15)
usecases.why: Orders (Order = 0) and sales returns are documented writes (pp. 13–15) and GetCustomers is limited to the salesman's customers by default (p. 7), but orders cannot be edited or cancelled through the API, a retried post may duplicate (no idempotency is documented), and the required fields and whether Shamel checks stock or credit limits are not stated.

usecases.title: Collections (receipts) app
usecases.description: Lets salesmen and collectors record cash and cheque payments from customers in the field, with bank, branch, cheque number and due date, and gives the customer an instant receipt.
data: receipt (type 24) header: customer_code, salesman, currency, rate, cheq_balance (p. 13)
cheques: cheq_num, account_num, bank_code, branch_code, due_date, currency, amount (p. 14)
customer balance before and after (p. 8)
usecases.why: Receipt = 24 and the cheque lines are documented (pp. 14–15), but the manual does not say where the cash part of a receipt goes (balance, an accounts line or elsewhere) or whether Shamel computes the totals, and a duplicated receipt cannot be deleted through the API.

usecases.title: Delivery & van-sales app
usecases.description: Shows a salesman or driver the delivery (load) prepared for them, lets them invoice customers from that load and record returns, and reconciles what is left in the van.
data: prepared delivery: header, items, cheqs (p. 16)
invoice from a delivery via delivery_id and delivery_pos (pp. 13–14)
return from a consignment delivery (type 5) (p. 15)
van stores via car_code (p. 6)
usecases.why: GetDelivery returns one Voucher 'prepared to the salesman' with no inputs (p. 16), so the result with zero or several prepared deliveries is unknown; 'invoice from a delivery' is listed (p. 3) but has no voucher type of its own, and both using SalesInvoice with delivery_id/delivery_pos and reading car_code as a van store are inferences.

usecases.title: Customer map & route planner
usecases.description: Plots each salesman's customers on a map with their balance and stopped status, so supervisors can plan daily routes and see areas that are poorly covered.
data: latitude, longitude, city, city_name, town, street, salesman_code, stopped (p. 7)
balance with getBalance (p. 7)
city names (p. 6)
usecases.why: latitude, longitude, city and salesman_code are documented customer fields and getAll returns every salesman's customers (p. 7); the caveats are that coordinates are strings that may be empty, town has no lookup list, and salesman names depend on the undocumented GetSalesmen (p. 6).

usecases.title: Field updates to customer records
usecases.description: Would let salesmen correct a customer's phone or address, capture the shop's GPS location, or mark a customer as stopped, directly from their phone.
data: latitude, longitude, phone, street, stopped (p. 7), readable but not writable
usecases.why: There is no customer update endpoint: Customer/Post only inserts new customers (p. 8) and its write model has no latitude, longitude or stopped field (p. 9), so corrections and GPS captures can only be queued in the tool for office staff to enter in Shamel.

usecases.title: Website catalogue & stock sync
usecases.title_ar: مزامنة الكتالوج والمخزون مع الموقع الإلكتروني
usecases.description: Publishes items with names, groups, prices, images and availability to the company website or a marketplace and keeps them in step with Shamel automatically, while Bawaba hides cost prices and GL accounts.
data: item code, name, nameEn, unit1, barcode, sale_parice1..sale_parice6, stopped, item_group_code (pp. 9–10)
item group tree (p. 11)
item_code and image_path (p. 11)
quantity per store (p. 11)
changes since a date via lastupdatedate (pp. 9–10)
usecases.why: Items, groups and stock are documented, but lastupdatedate is a date-only 'updated after' filter with no deletion signal (pp. 4, 9), the image_path format is undocumented and no endpoint returns image bytes (p. 11), so the sync must re-read with overlap and images stay off until ISCO explains them; M3 events later replace the polling.

usecases.title: Online orders into Shamel (web-shop & B2B portal)
usecases.title_ar: إدخال الطلبات الإلكترونية إلى الشامل (متجر إلكتروني وبوابة تجّار)
usecases.description: Turns orders from the company's web-shop, or from a portal where retail shop owners log in to see their own prices and balance, into Shamel sales orders, carrying the web order number so each order can be traced.
data: order (type 0) with manual_code holding the web order number (p. 13)
new web customers via Customer/Post (p. 9)
customer prices and balance for the portal (pp. 7, 16–17)
order status back to the buyer (p. 16)
usecases.why: Order insert is documented (pp. 13–15) and manual_code can carry the web reference (p. 13), but there is no idempotency, so a retried web order may duplicate, the purpose of system_id ('value must be between 1000 and 2000', p. 14) is unknown, status can be read back only by manual code (p. 16), and anonymous web buyers must be mapped to a Shamel customer account.

usecases.title: Event-driven notifications & integrations
usecases.title_ar: إشعارات وتكاملات فورية مبنية على الأحداث
usecases.description: Sends WhatsApp, email or Slack messages and pushes data to other systems when something changes: an order becomes ready, an item's stock drops, a customer's balance changes, or a new invoice or customer appears.
data: Bawaba events derived by polling: order.status_changed, stock.changed, customer.balance_changed, voucher.created, customer.created, item.updated
usecases.why: Shamel documents no push or webhook mechanism, so Bawaba's M3 events come from polling every 5 minutes and comparing results; lastupdatedate is date-only and exists on only three endpoints (pp. 7, 9, 10), deletions are never signalled, and GetVouchers filters only by a date range whose basis is unstated (p. 17), so events arrive with a delay.

usecases.title: Management KPI dashboard
usecases.description: One page for the owner with sales against last month, collections, total receivables, returned cheques, stock value by store and an estimated gross margin by item group.
data: sales and receipts by date from vouchers (pp. 13–15, 17)
receivables and cheque balances (pp. 7–8)
stock quantities times purchase_price (pp. 9–11)
line prices against purchase_price for margin estimates (pp. 9–10, 14)
usecases.why: Receivables and stock quantities are documented (pp. 7–11), but sales and collections depend on scanning GetVouchers without a type filter (p. 17), stock value and margin depend on purchase_price, whose meaning (last cost or average cost) is not stated (pp. 9–10), and multi-currency totals rely on only the latest 10 rates (p. 5).

usecases.title: BI export to Excel / Power BI
usecases.title_ar: تصدير البيانات إلى Excel وPower BI
usecases.description: Nightly export of customers, items, stock, balances and vouchers into Excel, Google Sheets, Power BI or a small data warehouse, so analysts can build their own reports without touching Shamel.
data: master data tables (pp. 4–11)
voucher headers and lines by date range (pp. 13–14, 17)
customer balances (pp. 7–8)
usecases.why: Master data exports are straightforward, but no endpoint documents paging, totals or row limits, voucher reads are limited to date ranges with no type filter (p. 17), and edits or deletions of vouchers are not signalled, so the warehouse must re-scan recent periods every night, and response sizes for long ranges are unknown.

usecases.title: Salesman performance & commission
usecases.description: Ranks salesmen by sales, returns, collections and new customers each month and calculates commissions with the company's own rules.
data: header salesman on invoices, returns and receipts (p. 13)
customer salesman_code (p. 7)
salesman list (p. 6, response undocumented)
usecases.why: VoucherHeader.salesman is documented (p. 13), but GetVouchers cannot filter by salesman or type (p. 17), the response of GetSalesmen is not documented at all (p. 6), and whether vouchers are salesman-scoped for a salesman user is unknown; new customers can only be found by comparing customer lists over time, because no creation date is returned.

usecases.title: AI assistant for customers & stock (read-only)
usecases.title_ar: مساعد ذكي للاستعلام عن الزبائن والمخزون (قراءة فقط)
usecases.description: A chat assistant (for example in WhatsApp or Teams) that answers staff questions such as 'what does this customer owe?', 'how many of this item are in the main store?' or 'is this serial still under warranty?' using a read-only Bawaba token.
data: customer cards and balances (pp. 6–8)
items, prices and stock per store (pp. 9–11)
serials and warranty dates (pp. 11–12)
usecases.why: Customer, balance, item, stock and serial questions map to documented lookups by code (GetCustomers code, getItemDetails itemCode, GetItemsSerials serial; pp. 6–12); questions about sales history inherit the GetVouchers limits (p. 17), and search by name is done by Bawaba over a full download because Shamel has no name-search parameter.
